# ms: # One successful turn under `kilo run`, from process start.
# The lane comes from chat.message (work start), the state-shaped
# session.status assertions, and session.idle (turn complete). session.created
# carries the session id the pane is bound by.
# The two rows that decide the port are the session.status ones. `status` is
# recorded here as `properties.status.type`, because that is where kilo puts the
# discriminator: the shipped schema is a union of {type:"idle"}, {type:"busy"},
# {type:"retry",...} and {type:"offline",...}. Herdr's kilo asset at integration
# version 4 accepts a status only when `typeof status === "string"`, so on this
# release it maps none of them and re-reports the session instead. Sidecar's
# asset reads `status?.type`, which is what Herdr's own opencode asset at
# session.status busy also repeats three times inside the one turn, which is why
# the asset suppresses an exact repeat of the lane it last reported: each report
# is a subprocess, not a socket write.
